questions.question: Eight athletes Sunil, Abhishek, Mohit, Cheenu, Rahul, Tanu, Koyal and Ankit are sitting around a circular table facing opposite to the centre (not necessarily in the same order). Koyal is third to the left of Rahul. Tanu is third to the right of Cheenu. Mohit is second to the right of Sunil. Abhishek is second to the left of Cheenu. Tanu is second to the left of Sunil. Who is sitting second to the right of Cheenu?
questions.solution:
Given: Eight athletes Sunil, Abhishek, Mohit, Cheenu, Rahul, Tanu, Koyal and Ankit are sitting around a circular table facing opposite to the centre.

1) Tanu is third to the right of Cheenu.

2) Tanu is second to the left of Sunil.

3) Abhishek is second to the left of Cheenu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a6648b9677eaecc2d348532a26a6e60c3a05ee597ced17bb0f90964f041caf28.png] 

4) Mohit is second to the right of Sunil.

5) Koyal is third to the left of Rahul.

After positioning Mohit, Koyal and Rhaul only one position is left which will be occupied by the only athlete left i.e Ankit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3ce8f0dc80becb859d7a7661cfa104a57d64358422a2b5058344487a71840f2d.png] 

Thus, according to the final arrangement Ankit is sitting second to the right of Cheenu.

Hence, "Option 3" is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. Some T are Y.

II. All Y are Z.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some Z are not Y.

II. Some Z are T.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a70754238aa1c377abea47983fede2f0073b6c77d98206fdebcac9c8ebcd27f.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some Z are not Y → Does not follow (As all Y are Z. So it is possible but not definite.)

II. Some Z are T → Follow (As some T are Y and all Y are Z. As some part of T is common with Y which whole comes in Z, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion II follows.

Hence, "Option 3" is the correct answer.
